claims.text: Annealing an as-cast MnNiSi-based magnetic refrigerant at approximately 600 °C for 1 hour under argon will induce Ni-rich nanoprecipitates.
The induced Ni-rich precipitates will be well dispersed, coherent with the MnNiSi matrix, and smaller than 15 nm.
Controlled cooling after annealing will prevent precipitate coarsening.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can strengthen an alloy by hindering dislocation motion.
The proposed Ni-rich nanoprecipitates will retard crack propagation in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Precipitation strengthening by the proposed nanoprecipitates will increase tensile or yield strength.
The proposed treatment will improve ductility relative to the as-cast MnNiSi-based alloy.
Magnetic strengthening defects can pin magnetic domain walls and thereby degrade magnetic properties.
Nanoscale precipitates smaller than the magnetic-domain-wall thickness can have little interaction with domain walls.
Fine, coherent nanoprecipitates can provide substantial strengthening while causing only a small deterioration in magnetic properties.
Fine, coherent Ni-rich precipitates will preserve the first-order magnetostructural transition of the MnNiSi-based alloy.
The magnetocaloric entropy change after annealing will remain within 10–15% of the as-cast value.
The magnetic transition temperature after annealing will remain within 10–15% of the as-cast value.
The as-cast MnNiSi-based baseline has a large magnetocaloric effect.
The as-cast MnNiSi-based baseline has insufficient strength and ductility.
Higher annealing temperatures, longer annealing times, or uncontrolled cooling may cause precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency.
Precipitate coarsening, loss of coherency, or annealing-induced phase transformations may alter the magnetic transition and reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
